name: tutorial-panel
purpose: The guide that runs tutorials beside the real product. It lives in the page's tools or help region, lists the tutorials a reader can take, and while one runs it shows the tutorial's tasks and the reader's place in them. The steps themselves happen on the page: each step points at a `TutorialPanelHotspot` placed beside the real control, and the current step opens there in a popover. `TutorialPanel.Provider` wraps the whole page (the content and the tools region), holds the running tutorial and the current step, and is what the panel and every hotspot read. A tutorial starts on a reader's action (the panel's Start); only one step is open on a page at a time. It is the stateful layer over `help-panel`: the panel is a `HelpPanel` with its `Header`, and draws each tutorial with its own internal task list (6.0 moved the former `HelpPanel.TutorialPanelTutorial` and `HelpPanel.Task` here; `HelpPanel` no longer has a tutorial mode). Design call (M2.9, WP app-layout): neither the design sample nor the Console Kit has a guided tutorial, so the model is Cloudscape's tutorial panel, hotspot and annotation context, rebuilt on WebKit parts. Design call (2026-11-18): the hotspot is a part of this component, not a component of its own. It renders nothing without the provider's running tutorial and reads only this component's context, so it belongs to this family the way Atlassian's `SpotlightTarget` belongs to its onboarding `SpotlightManager`; Shepherd.js and Driver.js have no separate target component at all (a step names its element), and the standalone hotspots of Appcues and Pendo work without a tour, which ours never does. Cloudscape ships `Hotspot` as its own export, but it too only works inside its annotation context. It is a companion part (it composes `Popover`), so it is imported on its own and not attached to the compound.
useWhen: Use TutorialPanel for guided tutorials whose steps point at real controls through TutorialPanelHotspot.
A reader learns a product task by doing it on the real screen, step by step, with the instructions pointing at the control they need next.
A product offers several tutorials in its help region and records which ones the reader finished.
A first-run or onboarding flow guides the reader through a real create and deploy, not a mock.
avoidWhen: Static help beside the page, with no guided run → use `help-panel`.
The step rail of a multi-step task in the app → use `stepper`, or `wizard` for a create flow with its footer.
A multi-step create flow whose steps are forms in one surface → use `wizard`.
Ordered steps the reader navigates inside a page → use `stepper`.
A single tip pinned to one control → use `popover` or `hint`.
An empty page that needs one call to action → use `empty-state`.
related: `help-panel` — the parts the panel draws with; use it alone for help without a guided run.
`popover` — what a `TutorialPanelHotspot` opens; the step's title, content and Previous / Next live in it.
`drawer` — the host of the tools region on narrow screens; the panel goes inside it.
bestPractices: Wrap the whole page in `TutorialPanel.Provider`, so the panel and every hotspot share one state.

Start a tutorial on a reader's action (the panel's Start, or a call to action that sets `activeKey`), never by presetting `activeKey` on the page's first render: a step popover over the page before the reader asked for it hides what they came to read.
One step is open on a page at a time. When a provider starts or moves a tutorial it takes the open step, and the step another provider had open closes (its marker stays and reopens it).

Keep tutorials as data (`TutorialPanelTutorial[]`): the panel lists them and the hotspots on the page read the same steps. This is the one place a config array is right — the step content is shown away from where it is declared.
One step, one control. Write the step title as the action (`Name the service`) and the content as one or two sentences.
Place every `TutorialPanelHotspot` a tutorial names on the page that runs it. A step whose hotspot is missing still shows in the panel, and focus moves to it there.
Set `completed` on a tutorial from what the product recorded (the `complete` event), not from a click.
Bind `v-model:activeKey` and `v-model:step` and persist them when a tutorial must survive a navigation.

props.name: title
props.doc: The panel's heading. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Tutorials`).

props.name: description
props.doc: One line under the heading. Empty uses the locale catalog.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name for the panel's landmark. Empty uses the title.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Renders skeleton lines in place of the content while the tutorials load.

slots.name: completion
slots.notes: Extra content on the completion screen, such as a feedback link.
